en: The Mahāvaipulya Daśacakra Sūtra, Scroll One.
Translator’s name lost; now appended to the Northern Liang Record.
1. Introduction, Chapter One.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Buddha was staying on Mount Kharatīya at the abode of the sage Muni, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and an immeasurable, incalculable multitude of śrāvakas;
there were also immeasurable, boundless, and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as he had finished preaching the *Candragarbha-sūtra*.

At that time, from the south, there arose great clouds of incense raining down great rain of incense; great clouds of flowers raining down great rain of flowers; immeasurable clouds of necklaces raining down various kinds of necklaces; and great clouds of robes raining down great rain of robes.
Upon Mount Kharatīya, at the dwelling place of the Muni seers, all these great rains completely filled the air.
From the vast clouds, there fell showers of fragrant flowers, garments, and necklaces, while various and immeasurable sounds of the Dharma were proclaimed.

In this manner, proceeding in sequence, there were sounds of the extensive exposition of the three refuges, sounds of upholding the precepts, sounds of patience, sounds of diligence, sounds of meditative concentration, and sounds of being endowed with wisdom; sounds of subduing the four Māras;
sounds of fame widely heard and filling the triple world; and sounds of mindfulness, concentration, and dhāraṇī, as well as emptiness.

The sound of signlessness and wishlessness; the sound of detachment from desire; the sound that form is like a mass of foam, sensation is like a water bubble, perception is like a mirage, mental formations are like a plantain tree, and consciousness is like an illusion;
the sounds of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self; the sound of shame and remorse; and the sound of the foundations of mindfulness.
The sound of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; the sound of realizing all dharmas; the sound of nirvāṇa;
the sound of having no dwelling place; the sound of the three vehicles; the sound of turning the wheel of Dharma; the sound of maturing sentient beings;
the sound of crossing over the three evil realms; the sound of the six pāramitās; and the sounds of skillful means up to the fulfillment of the ten stages.
The sound of the play of supernatural powers, the sound of the play of the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, the sound of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*),
the sound of the endurance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and the sound of entering the ocean of Buddhas.
The entire great assembly saw various kinds of rains and heard the sounds of immeasurable dharmas, as well as the sounds of garments and ornaments appearing according to their wishes.

Furthermore, they all saw that from both hands there rained down wish-fulfilling jewels (*cintāmaṇi*), each of which emitted radiance; within these lights, they beheld all the Buddhas of the worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, with each Buddha surrounded by his own bodhisattvas.
Within that radiance, one sees all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions. If there are those who are ill, when they are touched by the light, their myriad ailments are healed.
All those who are bound in fetters or destined for death, upon being touched by the light, attain liberation.
If one has committed evil through body, speech, or mind, at the moment the light touches the body, these three evils are entirely eliminated.
If sentient beings who are hungry and thirsty are touched by this light, they shall all become fully satiated;

those who undergo various punishments and suffer physical affliction, or who lack clothing, ornaments, necklaces, and various other necessities, shall have all their needs fulfilled according to their thoughts and recollections upon being touched by the light;

and if there are those who commit killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, frivolous speech, double-tongued speech, harsh words, or verbal abuse, all such evils shall be completely eliminated upon being touched by the light.
If there are sentient beings who suffer from the pain of not obtaining what they seek, once their bodies are touched by this light, they all experience joy.

This radiance is pure and entirely free from obscurations—such as wind, clouds, dust, and mist—as well as foul odors and impurities; all bitter afflictions, harsh and unwholesome sounds, and even fears and unpleasant tactile sensations are utterly extinguished.

They are distanced from all evils, and all forms of deceit, falsehood, and crookedness are eliminated without remainder; all evil desires are completely cast aside, and every kind of wondrous and supreme bliss gathers together.
At that time, the entire assembly was steadfast, as immovable as the earth; their minds were free from coming and going and could not be destroyed.
This great multitude attained what they had never experienced before, wondering: "By what cause and condition have our bodies now all become so heavy that we cannot support ourselves?"
At that time, there was a Śakra named Viśuddha who sat not far from the great assembly.
Then Viśuddha rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and questioned him in verse:
"O Speaker of Truth, Seer of Reality, The Muni, the Honored One, who dwells in reality; [Please explain] the meaning of this teaching."
Abiding long in the practice of the Dharma, we pray that you will expound the Teaching.
The Buddha is the true cause and condition who can extinguish the suffering of sentient beings;
for what reason does he rain down various kinds of rain in this place?
The great assembly was filled with joy, their hearts giving rise to faith and peace;
he dispelled all their doubts and led them to abide in the Mahāyāna.
His body remained as immovable as the earth, as did all the humans and devas.
All saw such signs, and the great assembly was filled with doubt.
From each of his two hands there issued forth the radiance of *maṇi* jewels,
as well as all kinds of garments, garlands, and various ornaments for adorning the body.
The field of merit for the ten directions, Free from all faults and evils;
Where all sufferings find rest— All this is due to the Savior of the World.
Among all devas and humans, None are able to describe his causes and conditions.
By whose supernatural power have you come to this place?
Are you a Buddha, a bodhisattva, Brahmā, Māra, Śakra, or one of their kind?
We pray that the Savior of the World will explain the causes and conditions of this supernatural manifestation.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Pure Abodes, saying: "So it is, so it is!
Listen attentively now!"
I shall now explain this.
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha has come here for the sake of maturing sentient beings in the world of the five turbidities throughout immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas;

he is accompanied by eighty *bimbara* nayuta hundreds of thousands of billions of great bodhisattvas, all of whom have come for the purpose of paying homage, making offerings, and showing reverence, desiring to see the assembly of the great multitude, and desiring to hear the great multitude give rise to sympathetic joy.

"This is the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha manifesting in the form of a śramaṇa, having produced such great adornments through the exercise of his supernatural powers; it is also the inconceivable and immeasurable merit of the Tathāgata;
it is called the 'Right Dharma Treasury' of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas;
and it is called the 'Great Jewel Island' of the treasure of liberating wisdom."
It is also called the Bodhisattva’s Dharma for Saving the World;
it is also called the Guide to Nirvana and the Caravan Leader.
It is like a wish-fulfilling jewel that satisfies all that is sought.
It is like a jewel island toward which all merchants journey;
it is like the great earth that can give rise to roots of goodness;
it is also the sacred vessel for the Great Dharma of Nirvana.
It is also a vessel for the purity of merit;
it is also the sphere of illumination for the sun and moon;
and it is also a great torch for the darkness of deep obscurity.

Like the moon, it is cool and removes the heat of afflictions; like one without feet obtaining a wish-fulfilling vehicle; like one with a distracted mind attaining the taste of ambrosia; like a frail elder encountering a stool and a staff—it is the very foundation of the great field of merit.

The mind of relinquishment is unimpeded like a deep-flowing current; it rescues from suffering as easily as visiting a kinsman. It is a great canopy of clouds that extinguishes the flames of the fetters (*saṃyojana*); like a water-purifying gem, it can remove turbidity and impurity. For those treading dangerous paths, it shows the way back to the correct road; for those who are utterly exhausted, it is a bed of peace and security. It is a bridge over the four currents of birth and death, and also the supreme great ship for crossing to the other shore.
It is the sublime and wondrous fruit of the three roots of goodness, and the most excellent Mahāyāna for all who practice giving.

Their observance of the precepts is as immovable as Mount Sumeru; their diligence is as indestructible as a diamond; their patience is as firm and solid as the great earth; they uphold the True Dharma with a mind free from dualistic marks; their meditative concentration is adorned like a wondrous flower garland; their wisdom is as deep and vast as the great ocean; their minds have no point of dependence, like empty space; and their skillful means are untainted, like a cluster of various flowers.

He stands among the followers of external paths like a lion king; he remains far removed from afflictions like the single horn of a rhinoceros; he extinguishes all fetters and latent tendencies like washing away dust and grime; and he is able to dispel foul odors like a swift, blowing wind.

In caring for those who are ill, he is like a skilled physician; in eliminating myriad ailments, he is like a wondrous king of medicines; in severing the fetters of all afflictions, he is like one wielding a sharp sword; to those who are terrified, he is a great friend; in warding off all enemies, he is like a fortified city with its moats; in removing their thirst, he is like pure water; in rescuing those who are hungry and destitute, he is like sweet fruit; he is the most excellent garment for the naked, and a dense cloud-canopy for those scorched by intense heat.

Possessing such fruits of these roots of goodness, which are supremely pure, firm, and indestructible, they are able to generate love and joy for subtle forms. They give rise to a sense of shame and remorse within great assemblies; they eliminate all fetters and afflictions as their sphere of meditative concentration. They ride upon the swift current of the four right efforts and the four means of integration; their earth of patience is like Mount Sumeru; their dhāraṇīs are as deep and vast as the great ocean; and their supernormal powers are unimpeded and sovereign throughout space. Having subdued all Māras and all habitual tendencies, they practice the right path and immeasurable meditative concentrations, serving as an island of omniscience, and are able to turn the unconditioned, pure wheel of Dharma.
“The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha has manifested these auspicious signs beforehand because he wishes to come; he has also come here for the purpose of making offerings to and honoring me.”
The Buddha again praised Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying:

"You have come from the south; eighty *bimbara* hundreds of thousands of *nayuta* bodhisattvas have all arrived here together by means of their supernormal powers. They have all assumed the appearance of *śrāvakas* before the Tathāgata, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and then, with palms joined, spoke these verses:
'O Supreme Teacher among the two-legged ones, You constantly cultivate loving-kindness and give rise to a virtuous mind;'"
Able to give rise to patience like the great earth, Liberating sentient beings and removing their anger;
Fully endowed with the greatest marks and signs of excellence, Able to adorn all realms;
Able to fulfill all fields of merit, Constantly practicing truthful speech and great compassion.
They are able to completely sever all nets of craving and dwell perfectly in accordance with reality;
they abandon other pure Buddha-fields where sentient beings already possess roots of goodness.
By original vow, you sought to deliver the turbid and evil world, To bring all sentient beings to maturity;
You were able to give rise to firm and diligent vigor, Surpassing immeasurable ascetic practices.
Constantly practicing what is difficult to do in terrifying places, he transcends immeasurable ascetic hardships;
through generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and diligence, he cultivates meditative concentration and wisdom.
They made offerings to countless Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as the great assemblies of Śrāvakas;
they provided sustenance for the hungry and thirsty and medicinal decoctions for the sick, delivering all beings from every form of bondage.
From time immemorial I have renounced body and life, Seeking no greed or regret for the benefit of sentient beings;
Constantly sacrificing my body for the sake of the Dharma, I give skin, bone, blood, and flesh to all beings.
Having relinquished all the pleasures they have attained for the sake of all beings through great compassion,
they practice the cultivation of quiescence and completely transcend the web of afflictions of all sentient beings.
Shutting down all six sense faculties, one is always able to remain far removed from all desires;
practicing the contemplations of suffering, impermanence, emptiness, and non-self, one also skillfully examines conventional truth.
The root cause of all suffering is craving; one who can completely dry up all afflictions thereby restrains the six sense faculties and is able to skillfully sever all desire.
Able to cultivate the gateways of immeasurable great compassion, universally bestowing [benefits] upon all sentient beings;
I shall not abandon my original vow, yet I shall likewise not dwell in supreme bodhi.
All sentient beings possess the mark of suchness, yet one also sees the masses of the blind suffering most acutely;
contemplating thus for the sake of sentient beings, one is then able to diligently cultivate great vigor.
Exerting diligence, generosity, ethical discipline, and patience, Cultivating all meditative concentrations and wisdom;
Just as a mother toward her only child, She nurtures them with a heart of loving-kindness.
You are likewise toward all sentient beings, Always able to provide for and sustain them all;
Therefore, you shall swiftly attain Bodhi And deliver all immeasurable multitudes.
When you originally cultivated the path to enlightenment, you vowed never to abandon a single sentient being;
there was none whom you did not establish in giving, ethical discipline, and patience, nor in diligence, meditative concentration, and the cultivation of wisdom.
Constantly able, within that final age, to seek the unsurpassed, supreme Bodhi;
for this reason, one shall rescue the world during the final kalpa and swiftly attain the unsurpassed, most excellent Path.
Subduing the evil Māras, yakṣas, and others, As well as all wicked nāgas, spirits, and humans;
Just as a vajra severs all fetters, They are able to establish all beings securely in the noble paths.
He bestows predictions upon immeasurable multitudes that they shall attain the unsurpassed path of Bodhi;
this one of supreme merit and brilliant wisdom is the great general of the true field of merit.
To save the world throughout immeasurable realms, you universally shelter all living beings;
acting as a field of merit across the worlds of the ten directions, your fame is heard afar, pervading everywhere.
Therefore, all these bodhisattvas, having completely set aside their own affairs, have gathered here by means of your supernormal power;
together they approach the World-Honored One, the Great Muni.
“May the Tathāgata please expound [the Dharma] at this time, so that all who hear it may rejoice;
having heard the Dharma, may they apply themselves with diligent effort and constantly cultivate and study the path to Bodhi.”
"It is entirely due to the power of you, the Great General, that we shall swiftly draw near to Bodhi;
never before have we heard of or seen such a great assembly as this, and for this reason you all have come together to this gathering."
There were thirteen billion yakṣas, who were extremely cruel and consumed flesh and blood;
having swiftly abandoned all evils, they arrived here and dwell securely in the most supreme and unsurpassed path.
Some have attained the dharani of patience; some have attained the most sublime meditative concentrations;
some have already realized the exhaustion of all outflows—these are the Arhats, free from attachment, honored among men.
There are those who can skillfully cultivate the four immeasurables, And those who can abide in the four means of integration;
There are those who have attained the four supreme eloquences, And others who have attained the cultivation of the various dharmakṣāntis.
Some have attained the Śūraṅgama samādhi; some have attained the wisdom-eye of space;
some have attained the patience regarding the non-arising of all phenomena—all because of the Dharma taught by the World-Honored One.
He has completely subdued all heterodox teachers, including the ninety-six kinds of non-Buddhist paths;
having crushed and humbled all demonic adversaries, this is entirely due to the power of the Great General who saves the world.
“Closing the gates of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, Benefiting all the multitudes of devas and humans;
Therefore, all true sentient beings Have gathered here through the Buddha’s spiritual power.”
The kalpas of famine, pestilence, and warfare are all extinguished this very day;
those sentient beings who are blind, ignorant, and have lost the right path, may they all be set free.
Those who were deranged by immeasurable afflictions have all been established upon the path of quiescent extinction;
the entire assembly has set aside their own karmic activities and come here for the sake of paying homage to the Tathāgata.
In immeasurable worlds and billions of buddha-fields, All are the abodes of those who save the world;
Their fame is renowned throughout the ten directions as immeasurable— Having heard this, we have come here.
To the ocean of merit of the knowledge of all modes, Who has heard such a true nature;
Who delivers all sentient beings— I now pay homage out of joy.
May I increase immeasurable virtues; therefore, I now bow my head in prostration.
Throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, may I always diligently practice various forms of giving.
I shall now train to give rise to the great vow; I have come here by the Buddha’s supernormal power.
I shall practice and train within this turbid world, Able to reach the foremost, supreme Bodhi.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha scattered various kinds of celestial flowers, fragrant blossoms, and necklaces over the Buddha; the flowers he scattered transformed into jeweled canopies.
At that time, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva was seated before the Buddha, listening to and receiving the Dharma.

The assembly gathered there, seeing Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, conceived a sense of rare wonder. They scattered various kinds of incense, flowers, necklaces, silk canopies, banners, pennants, and garments over Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying these words:
"We have truly gained excellent benefit; by the Buddha’s spiritual power, we have been able to see such great beings and pay them our respects and greetings."

At that time, there was also the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ke’ang (Thirsting with Longing), who rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"From which buddha-field has this son of good family come here?
What roots of goodness has he cultivated that he is able to offer such various praises and speak of the Buddha’s merits?"
"Since ancient times, I have never heard of or seen such a thing.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Thirsting for Aspiration: "Stop, stop!
"O Mahāsattva!
There is no need for this question.
Among all the great assemblies, as well as the devas and humans, there is none—save for the Buddha Tathāgata—who is able to know the measure of the merit of this son of good family."
The Tathāgata shall surely reveal this today; yet the devas and humans are obscured by their own ignorance and darkness.

This son of noble family has accomplished the inconceivable merit of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, entered the sphere of the Tathāgatas’ conduct, attained immeasurable dharmakṣānti, gained mastery over all Buddha-dharmas, and having entered profound dharmakṣānti, has crossed the ocean of omniscience.

This son of good family, sporting in the Lion’s Light Samādhi, ascends the summit of the Sumeru mountain of omniscience; he subdues heterodox teachers and brings sentient beings to maturity, dwelling in all Buddha-lands wherever they may be.
“Entering the Samādhi of Entering All Buddha-lands with Wisdom, by the power of this samādhi, he causes all sentient beings in all lands to see the bodhisattvas.
Entering the Samādhi of Joyful Entering All Buddha-lands with Wisdom, he partakes in all offerings made in those lands to worship the Buddhas.”

"Entering the Samādhi of Pure Joy according to the various Buddha-lands, upon entering this samādhi, one perceives all the faults and afflictions of every desire, yet the mental state remains pure and unstained."

"Entering the samādhi of shame and remorse in accordance with all Buddha-lands, he causes all sentient beings in those lands to fully attain shame and remorse, so that they remain far removed from all evils and are free from ignorance and darkness."
"Following the buddha-fields, they enter the *ābhāsvara* samādhi, and are also able to cause all those sentient beings to enter this same concentration;

they cause sentient beings to attain the knowledge of past lives (*pūrvanivāsajñāna*), enabling them to know how they died in previous lives and were born here, and becoming skilled in meditative absorption."
“Entering the Samādhi of Sorrowless Radiance in accordance with all lands, he is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to be entirely free from sorrow and grief.
Entering the Samādhi of Supernatural Powers in all Buddha-lands, he is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to enter the Samādhi of Supernatural Powers.”

"By entering the Samādhi of Wisdom-Light according to the Buddha-lands, one can also cause all sentient beings therein to be entirely free from ignorance, and thereby see all the Buddha-lands of the ten directions."
"Following the buddha-fields, he enters the Buddha-Torch Samādhi (*buddhāloka-samādhi*), and is likewise able to cause all sentient beings therein to return to that samādhi.

Following the buddha-fields, he enters the Vajra-Light Samādhi (*vajraprabhā-samādhi*); having entered this samādhi, he is also able to cause all those buddha-fields—the Iron Ring Mountains (*cakravāḍa*), the Great Iron Ring Mountains (*mahācakravāḍa*), and even Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains—as well as all ravines, gullies, and chasms—to become invisible, with the ground becoming as level as the palm of a hand;
and he is able to cause all venomous serpents and malevolent sorcery (*kṛtyā*) to be entirely extinguished."

"By entering the Samādhi of Entering All Buddha-lands through the Power of Wisdom and Subduing, one can also cause those Māras and their retinues to all be struck with terror and take refuge in the Triple Gem."

“Following the Buddha-lands, he enters the *vidyut-prabhā* samādhi, and is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to be free from fear of future lives and to attain the consolation of the Dharma.
Following the Buddha-lands, he enters the *rasa-rati* samādhi, and is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to have their every thought of food and drink fully satisfied.”

"Entering the Samādhi of Vital Energy and Joyful Delight in accordance with all Buddha-lands, he is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to attain firm bodies and be free from all suffering of illness."

“By means of the Samādhi of Entering All Buddha-lands to Enjoy the Requisites of Happiness, one can also cause all those sentient beings to fully obtain bedding, mattresses, clothing, and necklaces without any deficiency, as well as medicine for illness and emaciation, so that their bodies are all upright and handsome.”

"Following the various Buddha-lands, he enters the samādhi of non-contentious wisdom (*araṇā-jñāna-samādhi*), and is also able to cause all those sentient beings to have bodies that are tall, robust, dignified, and magnificent; to be far removed from all enmity, hatred, and bondage, and to attain happiness;
to delight in generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration with undistracted minds; and to be fully endowed with wisdom, deeply entering the Dharma-gates."
"Entering the Samādhi of Freedom from Sorrow and Fear in accordance with all Buddha-lands, he is able to cause all sentient beings therein to attain a heart of joy and be free from sorrow and fear."
"Entering the Samādhi of Radiant Joy in accordance with the various Buddha-lands, all sentient beings in those Buddha-lands attain unimpeded wisdom and are freed from worldly affairs.

Entering the Samādhi of the Well-Established Vajra in accordance with the various Buddha-lands, one can likewise cause all sentient beings therein to possess complete faculties, none of which are deficient or impaired."

"Following the buddha-fields, they enter the Samādhi of the Banner of Contemplation, and are likewise able to cause all those sentient beings to become weary of and renounce all evils, upholding the ten wholesome paths and ascending to the heavenly realms."

"By entering deeply into the Great Compassionate Sound Samādhi in accordance with the various Buddha-lands, one can also cause all those sentient beings to feel mutual pity for one another, giving rise to hearts of loving-kindness, attaining hearts free from fear, hearts free from affliction, and equanimous hearts, so that they further regard one another with compassion."

"Following the buddha-fields, he enters the Samādhi of the Gathering Place of Merit, and is also able to cause all those sentient beings to be free from strife, disease, famine, and unseasonable winds and rains; furthermore, the bitter, astringent, pungent, and sour flavors of their food and drink are all completely eliminated."

"This Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva enters the Samādhi of Oceanic Lightning wherever he goes; in whatever land he arrives, everything is transformed into a ground of jewels, free from all impurities and evils."
Garment trees, necklace trees, and flower-fruit trees adorn the Buddha-field.

At the time of dawn, he enters the *samādhi* of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; for the sake of maturing sentient beings, he arises from meditative concentration and causes immeasurable and boundless Buddha-worlds within the five turbidities and evil ages to have all sentient beings brought to fulfillment until none remain.
In a buddha-world where the calamities of war have arisen, by the power of this son of noble family entering samādhi at the break of dawn, all weapons, armor, and armaments are entirely extinguished.
"In accordance with whichever Buddha-lands where pestilential kalpas arise to harm sentient beings, may those epidemics be naturally eliminated.
In accordance with whichever Buddha-lands where famines arise, may those famines be completely extinguished and all [beings] obtain full sufficiency."
"This son of good family, by the majestic spiritual power of this samādhi, is able to bring all sentient beings to maturity.
Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha brings sentient beings to maturity through inconceivable merit."
In the presence of immeasurable Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the past, he long ago made firm vows of great compassion.

He has brought all sentient beings to full maturity; his power of adornment is like a thunderclap, and in the time it takes to eat a single meal, he can bring to maturity countless billions of nayutas of people, endowing them with roots of goodness.

"If there are sentient beings who, tormented by immeasurable billions of various sufferings and pressed by hunger and thirst, invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, he is able to cause them all to have their food and drink sufficiently provided and to extinguish all their sufferings, establishing them on the path to nirvāṇa so that they may all attain happiness."
"If there are sentient beings who lack clothing, jeweled crowns, necklaces, or various necessities such as medicine for the treatment of illness and emaciation—
if they invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, he shall cause them to be fully provided with whatever they desire, establishing them in the path of nirvāṇa and attaining the supreme bliss."

"If there are sentient beings who are separated from a mind of joy and happiness and are instead gathered with those who lack joy and happiness, should they invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, all instruments of joy and happiness will come to them, and that which they do not delight in will likewise be entirely removed;
as for what their hearts desire, they shall be able to attain it all, dwelling securely in nirvāṇa and obtaining the supreme bliss."

"If there are sentient beings whose bodies and minds suffer from various ailments and afflictions, should they be able to recite the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, all their physical and mental distress will be entirely healed and cured, and they will be established in nirvāṇa and attain the supreme bliss."

"If there are sentient beings who harbor evil intentions toward one another, yet can invoke the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and take refuge with single-minded devotion, I shall cause those beings to become gentle, patient, and mutually respectful; through a heart of compassion, they shall repent and abide in nirvāṇa."

"If there are sentient beings bound and imprisoned, their bodies shackled and fettered, undergoing all manner of suffering, and they are able to recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva with single-minded devotion and take refuge in him, I shall cause all those sentient beings to attain liberation, sovereignty, and unimpeded freedom."

Even those who are about to be bound, imprisoned, or flogged with whips and staves—if they can recite the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and take refuge in him with single-minded devotion—they shall likewise all be completely liberated, abide in nirvana, and attain the supreme bliss.

"If there are sentient beings whose faculties are incomplete, who are exhausted and indolent, deranged, dissolute, or have lost their original minds; and whose evils—such as greed, anger, ignorance, jealousy, stinginess, perverse delusion, arrogance, and sleep—all blaze intensely;

if they can recite the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and take refuge with single-minded devotion, all such sufferings shall be brought to liberation, and they shall dwell securely in nirvāṇa, attaining the supreme bliss."
“If there are sentient beings who are swept away by great floods, consumed by fierce fires, or who fall from high cliffs into perilous mountain precipices;

or who fall from trees and various dwellings and tumble to the ground—should they encounter such immeasurable terrors and invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha with single-minded devotion and take refuge in him, all such fearful matters shall be entirely liberated, and they shall abide in nirvāṇa and attain the supreme bliss.”

"If there are sentient beings who are bitten by various venomous snakes or diverse beasts, or those who have been struck by various poisons, should they be able to recite the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and take refuge with single-minded devotion, they shall all be liberated from these fears."

"If there are sentient beings who are obscured and harmed by an apasmāra [seizure], such that for one day, two days, three days, or even up to four days, it causes their minds to become deranged, disordered, trembling, agitated, inverted, or even leads to the loss of mind—

if such sons or daughters of noble family can recite the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and take refuge with single-minded devotion, they shall be completely liberated from all fears, dwell securely in nirvāṇa, and attain the supreme bliss."

“If there are sentient beings who are seized by various rākṣasas, evil spirits, kumbhāṇḍas, or piśācas; or by lions, tigers, wolves, or those practicing malevolent sorcery with poisonous poisons; or who are surrounded by enemy armies, combatants, or hostile thieves;

and who, facing the enemy, fear death and crave life, seeking only pleasure—if such sons or daughters of noble family can invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and take refuge in him with single-minded devotion, they shall quickly be freed from all sufferings, have all their afflictions and hardships eliminated, abide in nirvāṇa, and attain the supreme bliss.”

"If there are sentient beings who, for the sake of much learning, faith, precepts, giving, meditative concentration, supernormal powers, liberation; for the sake of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles; for the sake of various merits; for the sake of crafts, flowers, fruits, trees, and bedding; for the sake of increasing wealth and profit; for the sake of various medicines, dwellings, and houses; for the sake of causing rain and water to fall in season; for the sake of obtaining coolness; for the sake of seeking sons, daughters, wives, and concubines while practicing merit through skillful means; or for the sake of removing cold and heat to attain right mindfulness—they seek such various causes and conditions;..."

Any who can recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and take refuge with single-minded devotion—by virtue of this son of good family’s majestic power—shall be able to fulfill the merits and aspirations of those immeasurable sentient beings.
"Just as seeds sown in a wasteland can all be transformed into subtle and sublime fruits if one single-mindedly takes refuge by reciting the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha."

Why is this? Good son! Because in the past, throughout immeasurable, incalculable, and countless eons, before the Tathāgatas, he made firm vows like the great earth, so that all sentient beings might obtain their enjoyment.

By the power of the merit of these sons of good family, they are able to cause the roots of goodness—the sprouts, stems, branches, leaves, and even the flowers and fruits—to all become moistened, grow, and reach full maturity.

"If there are sentient beings who have committed various evils and the ten unwholesome karmas, yet are able to recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and take refuge with single-minded devotion, all their fetters, latent tendencies, and afflictions will be extinguished; they will distance themselves from the ten evils and accomplish the ten virtues, giving rise to a mind of compassion and a mind of benefit toward all sentient beings."

By the power of his diligence, these sons of good family, within the duration of a single meal, deliver and liberate immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) sentient beings—equal in number to the sands of the Ganges—in each and every one of the immeasurable, incalculable Buddha-worlds during that same interval of a single meal;
by means of such manifestations, they cause them to escape all evils and bring them to the full accomplishment of inconceivable merit.
This son of good family, by the power of such firm vows, is able to bring all sentient beings to maturity.

Thus, noble son, he may manifest in the body of Brahmā to accomplish the welfare of beings; or he may manifest as Maheśvara, Mahāmaheśvara, or Maheśvara-deva; or he may manifest as a deva of the desire realm, such as Paranirmita-vaśavartin, Nirmāṇarati, Tuṣita, or Yāma;

or as the body of Śakra, or the bodies of the Four Great Kings; or he may manifest as the body of a bodhisattva, or the body of a pratyekabuddha, or the body of a śrāvaka; or he may manifest as the body of a wheel-turning sage king (cakravartin), or as the bodies of brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras.

Sometimes he manifests in the body of a male or female; sometimes in the body of a boy or girl; sometimes in the body of a gandharva, kinnara, mahoraga, deva, nāga, or yakṣa; sometimes in the body of a rākṣasa, a kumbhāṇḍa, a piśāca, or a pūtana; sometimes in the body of a lion, or a tiger, a wolf, an elephant, or a horse; sometimes in the body of a water buffalo, or various kinds of birds; sometimes in the body of King Yama, or a hell-guardian, or a denizen of hell.

For the sake of all sentient beings, he preaches the Dharma in various ways, manifesting the three vehicles according to the needs of those beings, causing them all to abide in the stage of non-retrogression.
This son of good family has accomplished such an inconceivable treasury of merit and is adorned with the jewel of liberation;
he is the mother of all dharmas for the bodhisattvas and is heading toward great nirvana as an unsurpassed caravan leader.

“Good son! If there are great bodhisattvas such as Maitreya, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, Samantabhadra, and others who serve as leaders—bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—if a person were to pay homage and make offerings to them for a hundred kalpas in order to seek their wishes, it would not equal the merit gained by paying homage and making offerings to the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha for even the duration of a single meal; the latter’s merit is far greater, and all one’s wishes will be swiftly fulfilled.”
Why is this? Because this Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha is able to bring great benefit to all sentient beings as a wish-fulfilling jewel.
This son of noble family, if he wishes to bring sentient beings to maturity, can manifest the firm treasury of great compassion, thereby fulfilling the heart’s desires of all sentient beings.
"Therefore, sons and daughters of good family!
You should make offerings to the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

At that time, the great assembly gathered from the ten directions—bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, śrāvakas, and all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others—rose from their seats and made offerings according to their means.

Or they scatter fragments of gold, silver, and the like upon that Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha; or they scatter various kinds of precious flowers, garments, maṇi jewels, as well as flower garlands, pearl necklaces, and banners and canopies of golden thread upon the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha;
furthermore, they make offerings to the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha with immeasurable music and various hymns of praise.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha again presented this offering to the Sugata and spoke these verses:
“Offered by devas, humans, nāgas, and spirits, Bodhisattvas from the ten directions have all gathered;
Hearing that there is the great merit of saving the world, I pray that the Buddha accept my most excellent offering.”
At that time, after the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha had spoken these verses, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
“Those who wish to give rise to firm and pure wisdom Can extinguish all the afflictions of sentient beings.”
May you cause the multitude to attain happiness like the Jewel-Hand, and sever the web of fetters like a vajra.
Arise with great compassion and all forms of diligence; with these, make offering to the Most Victorious Honored One.
With a mind like the ocean that rescues all, ferry all sentient beings to the further shore beyond suffering.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha rose from his prostrations and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I shall deliver these four continents and cause the increase of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, [and upāsikās].”
O Upāsikā, you shall increase in protective mindfulness, increase in lifespan with a body free from illness,
increase in physical beauty and strength, increase in reputation, increase in resources and livelihood,
increase in kinsmen and friends, increase in retinue, increase in faith and precepts, increase in learning, and increase in generosity.
They increase patience; they increase skillful means; they increase the factors of enlightenment and the noble truths;
they increase entry into all the right paths of the Mahāyāna; they increase the illumination of the true characteristics of phenomena;
they increase the maturation of all sentient beings; and they increase the arousal of great loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity.
It increases all immeasurable pure dharmas; it increases wondrous renown and fame throughout the three realms;
it increases the rain of Dharma that moistens the streams of the three existences; it increases the essential flavors of all things upon the great earth;
it increases all the virtuous karma of sentient beings; it increases the fragrance of the Dharma and countless meritorious practices; it increases wisdom in its entirety.
It illuminates, increases the path practiced through the six pāramitās, increases the five eyes so they penetrate without obstruction,
increases empowerment, increases nirvāṇa, and increases majestic power that illuminates all unprecedented dharmas—
the mantras, dhāraṇīs, and chapters of incantations for the ultimate realization of all virtues.
In the past, in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I have received and upheld such mantras as these;

they increase the pure and complete dharmas, increase all medicinal herbs, grains, seeds, roots, stalks, flowers, and fruits, increase clouds, rain, earth, water, fire, and wind, increase merit and happiness, increase wealth and possessions, increase immeasurable and most excellent karmic rewards, and increase one's foundational estate. These mantras are beneficial, for they can eliminate all suffering, affliction, and bondage.

At that time, while the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha was extensively expounding this Mahāvyākaraṇa Sūtra, Mount Khadiraka shook in six ways; all musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck; a rain of various precious flowers fell; and the entire great assembly trembled with awe, giving rise to thoughts of the marvelous.

At that time, the goddess Guṇakāśikā, the goddess Guṇarati, the goddess Manojñasvarā, the goddess Dṛḍhāpṛthivīdevatā, the goddess Acintya, and the goddess Mahāprabha—these and other goddesses acting as leaders, together with eighteen thousand and other great Īśvara spirits, rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is rare, World-Honored One!”
"How marvelous, Sugata!

Although we have attained mastery over the four great elements, we are unable to know the fundamental causes and conditions for the arising and ceasing of the initial, middle, and final characteristics of these elements; we do not recognize enmity or affection, nor do we know what is wholesome or unwholesome, up to and including who our kinsmen and friends are."

If a son of good family attains this profound Prajñāpāramitā, he will be able to skillfully discern the initial, middle, and final characteristics of these four great elements and understand their various processes of arising and ceasing.
The Buddha said: “So it is, so it is! O Goddess!”
This son of good family has attained the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and skillfully understands the beginning, middle, and end of the four great elements (*mahābhūta*).
It is like a benevolent deity who possesses a wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*), which can rain down various immeasurable showers of jewels, bringing great benefit.
In this way, Good Goddess!
This son of good family is further able to rain down various kinds of immeasurable jewels of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*), bestowing them all universally upon all sentient beings.
"Just as a jewel island can produce immeasurable varieties of jewels,
so too it is with this son of good family, who fulfills the various jewels such as the factors of enlightenment (bodhipākṣika-dharma)."
For example, when the flowers of the pārijātaka tree first bloom, their light and color are wondrous and beautiful;
in the same way, a son of good family who adorns himself with the immeasurable Buddha-dharmas is likewise.
Just as the lion king cannot be startled by any living being,
so too, good son, does one attain fearlessness among all assemblies.
"Just as the rising sun destroys all darkness,
so too, noble son, is it with your ability to eliminate the darkness of all the crookedness, fetters, and latent tendencies of sentient beings."
Just as the bright moon illuminates the four continents, enabling those who are lost to regain the right path;

so too, good son, can you cause those who have not yet entered the Three Vehicles and are迷失 (lost) in the wilderness of birth and death to all turn back toward and attain the right path, abiding securely within the Three Vehicles.
"Just as the great earth causes all seeds of the hundred grains, as well as medicinal herbs and trees, and all sentient beings to grow and flourish;
so too, son of good family, do all other wholesome dharmas that assist the path attain growth."
"Just as Sumeru, the king of mountains, is well-established and firm, abiding so that all things neither increase nor decrease;

so too, son of good family, you should abide in the Buddha-dharma without abandoning any sentient beings, making your roots of goodness firm and without deficiency, ensuring they are not lost or leaked away."
"Just as all sentient beings rely upon and dwell within space as they walk, stand, enter, and exit;
so too, O noble son, do all sentient beings rely upon [this] to increase all their immeasurable merits."

At that time, the entire great assembly, upon hearing the name of this Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, gave rise to a sense of rarity and attained what they had never experienced before; with reverence and respect, they were all greatly delighted, gazing intently at Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha without casting their eyes away for even a moment.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
“The merits of the dhūtas are all in harmony; The assembly of śrāvakas shows no signs of difference.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha Has come here to pay homage to the World-Honored One.”
Having crossed over the various sufferings and afflictions of the three evil realms, they have come here to pay homage to the World-Honored One;
the devas everywhere rain down immeasurable kinds [of offerings], all for the sake of making offerings to the World-Honored One.
Then, observing clearly in the four directions, Śakra, Lord of Devas, free from defilement and illuminating with light,
joined his palms with a single mind toward the Buddha, desiring to exhort the World-Honored One.
I now wish to see this great assembly; The maṇi-jewel emits a brilliant light.
It is the most vast and expansive of all fields of merit; All behold its light shining everywhere.
The World-Honored One’s supernormal powers and radiant light shine forth; for whose sake has this manifestation appeared?
Among the great assembly gathered here, who is the most courageous?
Kṣitigarbha has arrived—a true son of the Buddha.
The hidden treasure is the perfect bestowal of the seven jewels; the Buddha-treasury is the precious jewel of fearlessness.
The seed is the Great Bodhisattva, the caravan leader for all sentient beings.
This Lord can give birth to the jewels of the Buddha-dharma; he is a sea of great merit and is diligent.
His essential nature is one of great compassion and he is most wise; he is able to rescue all sentient beings from suffering.
They can also deliver all who are terrified;
they can produce roots of goodness like the great earth, and like a vajra, they shatter all fetters.
They are great donors of the jewel of liberation, and they wash away all afflictions like a great flood of water.
Like a canopy that universally covers the heat of afflictions, and like a skilled physician who eliminates all maladies,
to praise Kṣitigarbha for even the duration of a single meal surpasses the merit of all bodhisattvas for ten billion kalpas.
Just as all wise ones possess immeasurable virtues, so does the Greatly Renowned Kṣitigarbha;
he causes all sentient beings bound by afflictions to distance themselves from them and attain liberation.
Having attained the Great Samādhi of Śūraṅgama, he is able to lead all through the various dhyānas to the further shore.
The twelve links of dependent origination are entirely pure, and his wisdom is as vast as space;
throughout immeasurable Buddha-lands, he is able to extinguish the mass of darkness for all sentient beings.
Throughout all four dhyānas, they universally observe the Buddha-lands and cultivate various practices;
they are able to lead sentient beings into samādhi, so that all may be freed from the fever of afflictions.
Due to the past evil karma of sentient beings, they constantly dwell in kalpas of swords, weapons, and pestilence;
suffering afflictions within this world, those good sons are able to rescue and liberate them.
All sentient beings within the six realms of existence, Constantly oppressed by suffering and affliction;
Should all take refuge in Kṣitigarbha, And cause all their suffering and affliction to be completely extinguished.
Sentient beings revolve in saṃsāra, submerged in various sufferings, mutually harming one another and giving rise to strife and contention;
if they can take refuge in Kṣitigarbha, he shall cause all such strife and contention to be entirely pacified through patience.
The three evil realms are most terrifying; there, one’s desires go unfulfilled and one suffers constant distress.
One should likewise take refuge in Kṣitigarbha, and all fears shall be eliminated.

If one cultivates the precepts and mindfulness-concentration, and desires to attain great learning and wisdom, one should take refuge in Kṣitigarbha; all that the heart desires shall be fully satisfied.
Those who wish to attain such merits, As well as the seeds of skillful arts,
Should all take refuge in Kṣitigarbha, So that their aspirations may be fully satisfied.
For all medicinal herbs, grains, and various fields of merit, and even for those who seek sons, daughters, and the like—
one should take refuge in Kṣitigarbha, so that their every aspiration may be fully satisfied.
If one wishes to cultivate all meritorious virtues, All things depend upon the great earth;
Just as medicinal herbs and grains flourish and are nourished, They likewise grow and increase by virtue of Kṣitigarbha.
Enshrouded and obstructed by the afflictions of karmic bonds, They commit the ten evils and all manner of unwholesome deeds;
All should take refuge in Kṣitigarbha, And all their fetters, compulsions, and grave transgressions shall be entirely eliminated.
Able to manifest the True Dharma to sentient beings, Assuming various forms to teach according to their needs;
Fully cultivating the merit of all kinds of giving, They give rise to great compassion, desiring to save all beings.
Even if one were to spend a full hundred kalpas, one could not fully discern their merit;
this is called the great treasury of merit, and all should offer worship to it.

3. Chapter on Questioning the Fundamental Karma and Severing the Ties of Defilement. The Buddha-spoken Mahāvaipulya Daśacakra Sūtra, Chapter Three: Questioning the Fundamental Karma and Severing the Ties of Defilement. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, knelt with his right knee on the ground and his hands joined in prayer, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
"As I now wish to pose a few questions, I pray that you will grant me leave; I would then like you to explain them for me at this time.
The Buddha said, "You are a truly virtuous man (satpuruṣa). You desire to manifest unimpeded wisdom for all sentient beings and also cause others to become great men (mahāpuruṣa)."
"If you have any questions, answer them according to your own inclination; do not harbor doubts or difficulties.
Today the Tathāgata shall provide an explanation for you, causing you to rejoice.
At that time, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva asked in verse:
"In thirteen kalpas past, I cultivated the Buddha-field;
during famines and epidemics, I extinguished them all for the sake of sentient beings.
For hundreds of millions of Buddhas and others, I created inconceivable offerings."
Now I see this great assembly gathered; the pure multitude has come together.
Wise and diligent, all have arrived at this gathering;
they have assembled like clouds at once, free from all turbidity and evil.
In this defiled age, there is much censure and suspicion; those who commit evil harm pure conduct.
Why do those with unwholesome discernment disturb and destroy dignified decorum?
They conspire with the wicked and rebellious, slandering the True Dharma.
They revile the various worthies and sages, falsely clinging to the views of annihilationism and eternalism.
They commit the ten unwholesome karmas, fearing not the suffering of future lives;
they destroy the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, and through flattery and crookedness, they head toward the evil realms.
Ignorance obscures their eyes, and greed and envy abound with deceit and falsehood;
how can you turn the Wheel of Dharma and liberate them from all such crookedness?
When afflictions and the vajra coexist, how can they be severed and abandoned?
What is meant by "dhāraṇī"?
Patience is able to bring about gentleness.
This accumulation of what has never occurred before has caused me to encounter the World-Leader.
Never before have I seen such a great assembly,
Perfect in the practice of dhūta, having long cultivated the path to enlightenment;
How is it that in this very place, You have attained Buddhahood and turned the wheel of Dharma?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:
"Excellent, excellent! O son of good family!"
In the past, at the abodes of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, you have already inquired about this meaning.
You have likewise heard such teachings before; endowed with the practice of wisdom and perfected in merit, you have crossed to the other shore by means of skillful power.

For the sake of accomplishing the peace, happiness, and benefit of all other sentient beings, and desiring to cause the assembly of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to fulfill the treasury of all skillful means; for the purpose of possessing the six pāramitās and desiring to fill the ocean of omniscience;

for the purpose of turning back kings and rulers so they do not fall into evil realms, and desiring to cause the Three Jewels to flourish throughout the worlds of the ten directions and for the True Dharma to abide for a long time—it is for these reasons that you question the Tathāgata.
"Good son! Listen now attentively, listen attentively!
I shall explain it for you."
Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"So be it, World-Honored One! I am eager and desirous to hear [your teaching]."
The Buddha said:

"This is the accomplishment of the Ten Wheels through the power of the Tathāgata’s original vows from the past; it is because in such lands there is an evil world of the five turbidities, wherein all pure dharmas are entirely diminished."
Far removed from the seven noble riches and distant from all wise people, they are shrouded and obstructed by the net of eternalism and nihilism.
Riding the chariot of the evil realms, they fear not the future life, dwelling perpetually within the dark gloom of ignorance.

They fully practice the ten evil deeds and are capable of committing the five heinous crimes; they slander the true Dharma and revile the worthy and holy ones, remaining far removed from all virtuous merits while accomplishing only unwholesome dharmas.

In such a world of manifold evils, they are able to bring all beings to peace and security so that they attain fearlessness; they accomplish the most supreme Dharma of the former sages, turn the wheel of the Dharma, and subdue all adversaries; they utterly conquer and destroy afflictions like a vajra, and cause all sentient beings to dwell securely in the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*) within the Three Vehicles.

“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who is devoid of merit; within his own realm or in a world-system, an army may arise, or he may be trampled and harmed by the powerful troops of a neighboring country coming from abroad.
They are afflicted by various anxieties, distresses, and conflicts; they suffer from manifold diseases such as flattery, hypocrisy, deception, and lying;
they are shrouded by ignorance and darkness so that their vision is unclear; they are possessed by *kumārabhūta* spirits and malevolent demons;
they are deluded and attached by *apasmāra* [seizure] spirits, their bodies withering away and their minds becoming deranged and lost.
Their faculties are ugly and their hands and feet are incomplete; they are constantly destitute of wealth and property, lacking in fortune and merit, and are not beloved by anyone.
They mostly take refuge in heterodox paths and give rise to various false views; with their minds inverted, they head toward the three evil realms.

In such a land, there are many elders who serve as ministers, officials, and administrators among the people; their ranks and emoluments are orderly, and they do not harm one another out of personal favoritism.

When a nation is established in this manner, there will be immeasurable and diverse enlightened regulations to discipline the people; they will be fully endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, loving-kindness, patience, and dignified deportment, and all difficult practices and ascetic austerities will be completely fulfilled.

By virtue of such causes and conditions of merit, the faculties of sentient beings will all be complete; their bodies will be tall and large, their majestic virtue blazing and intense, and their physical marks and signs will be upright and serene. They will always be respected and honored by all, and they will all be friends to one another, possessing a benevolent nature that is broad and compassionate, as well as being quick-witted and possessed of great wisdom.

If there are those who are honored, such as princes, who possess these virtues, they shall bathe with various fragrant waters, tempered to be neither too hot nor too cold, and put on fresh, clean garments that shine like jewels.

Upon their heads were further such jewel-encrusted golden flower garlands; their hands were bound with plain silk and various flower wreaths, while earrings and rings were made of gold, silver, and pearls. Their arms and fingers were adorned with nets of miscellaneous jewels, and they wore various bracelets and bangles—thus adorning their bodies with such treasures.
All the devas, sages, and Śakras whom he had previously served gave their full consent for the arrangement of the high throne,
just as when his father, the king, ascended the exalted position in the past.

Having ascended such a throne and succeeded to the royal position, all the dragon kings, the lord of the devas, the lord of the asuras, and the lord of the kumbhāṇḍas—these same bells and drums that belonged to his former father-king—are now struck upon this occasion of his accession to the throne.

Such sounds filled the cities and towns, and all the kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, and śūdras bathed their bodies, donned fresh and clean garments, and—with various jewels, silk canopies, banners, flags, gold, silver, maṇi-gems, pearls, coral, lapis lazuli, conch shells, and all manner of precious treasures—made diverse offerings because they saw such auspicious signs as these due to the installation of the new king.

"At that time, when the new king had succeeded to the position of consecration, the long-standing former ministers appointed by the previous king were assigned to their respective offices according to their capabilities.

Whether military mobilization arose within his own realm or enemy forces were raised by neighboring states, he utterly destroyed all hostile adversaries as they appeared; he protected his own kingdom without any damage and skillfully increased his retinue, making them mutually affectionate and friendly."
“Good son! If one can act in this way, it is called the first wheel of the consecrated royal station.
One shall dwell in peace and happiness within that realm, having first subdued all enemies; one’s lifespan shall be long, and one’s life and body shall be protected.”

"So it is, so it is! Good son, if people dwell in the evil worlds of the five turbidities and are far removed from the Buddha, for this reason all sentient beings therein have minds full of anger and mutually oppress one another, and all the populace is filled with grief and affliction."

Out of foolishness, darkness, and ignorance, they give rise to views of annihilationism and eternalism; they engage in various disputes, litigation, greed, envy, flattery, and hypocrisy; they commit all manner of deceptions and are fully possessed of the ten non-virtuous actions. Clinging to sentient beings, they trouble and disturb the populace with various afflictions and calamities. For this reason, they remain far removed from the profound eye of the Dharma and are afflicted by the malady of hatred.

Their minds constantly distance themselves from and abandon the true flavor of all dharmas; their thoughts are distracted as they revile the wholesome Dharma and delight in the flavors of what they crave; they are perpetually shrouded by the net of afflictions and various false views.
Those who take refuge in the six teachers ruin and destroy the Noble Path, heading toward the three evil realms.

Yet there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have already drawn near to and made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas of the past, who are able to cross the great ocean of all-encompassing wisdom, and who dwell securely in the path practiced by all Buddhas; they have all gathered together and come to my presence.

Through the cultivation and accumulation of various forms of giving, you have been well able to subdue yourself and accomplish ascetic practices, remaining far removed from all evils; for a long time, you have practiced the difficult austerities that are hard for all Buddhas to perform.

They constantly contemplate the vast treasury of ornaments consisting of wisdom, skillful means, merit, great kindness, and great compassion; they have fully perfected all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, and forbearances, as well as the great oceans of the various stages, and they give rise to no mind of flattery, deception, illusion, or falsehood.
Their physical forms are gentle and harmonious, perfected through the practice of patience; they are constantly adorned with virtuous compliance, drawing near to the ocean of all-knowledge.

Their complexions are magnificent and radiant, fully endowed with light, such that they can act as great guides for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and likewise provide consolation to all sentient beings who fear the terrors of birth and death.
These are the sons of the Tathāgatas such as Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, and Kāśyapa Buddha; they are the most preeminent leaders within this Bhadrakalpa.
They bathe themselves with the water of the wisdom of meditative concentration and don the robes of shame and remorse; this is the sphere of practice for the most supreme Great Sages.
It is also a garland of flowers of the merit of liberation, and is called the self-adornment of the reality of non-arising through all-knowledge.

Having formed a dense cloud-canopy for the three realms through these three types of wholesome conduct, they have attained secure dwelling in all Buddha-lands of the past and sit upon the seat of the vajra-samādhi.
It was also where, in the past, the seats of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas were established—the seats of the four foundations of mindfulness;
it is also the seat established by previous buddhas.

Abiding on the island of omniscience at the seat of enlightenment, they are able to turn the wheel of Dharma, ensuring that the lineage of the Triple Gem continues without interruption; they beat the drum of Dharma, producing a great sound that pervades the three realms.

By means of this sound of the Wheel of Dharma, may all devas, humans, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, as well as kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, pretas, and piśācas, all adorn themselves with the characteristic of the quiescence of the Four Noble Truths.

The wheel of Dharma with its three turnings and twelve aspects, which has never been turned before, is now turned by me; it cannot be turned by any śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa, nor by any deva, Māra, or Brahmā. This is for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all gods and humans.
“Good son! This is called turning the first wheel.
By knowing, as they truly are, what is possible and what is impossible regarding this life and future lives, one reaches a state of peace and fearlessness, wherein all enemies naturally submit.”
Knowing things as they truly are, he is able to turn the Brahma-wheel, manifesting throughout the five turbidities of the evil world.

His disciples rightly roar the lion’s roar; for those sentient beings who have committed the five heinous crimes or perfected the ten evil deeds, he shatters their afflictions like a vajra, severs all outflows to bring about liberation, and establishes them in the three vehicles according to their inclinations, dwelling on the stage of non-retrogression.

“Good son! It is like a person who has newly ascended the throne and, having received the consecration, examines the various and immeasurable royal affairs of the three periods of time—past, present, and future;
and by means of wisdom, he examines the causes of karma and all their resultant retributions, assigning ranks and positions according to their respective natures and characteristics.”
By means of these three types of action, they cause their own lands to increase in peace and happiness, while all neighboring enemies are utterly subdued.
What are these three?

They are like an anointed Kṣatriya king who, for the sake of protecting his life, prepares for battle against enemies, and manages the royal palace, the various territories, all stipends, and the livelihoods of the people.
This is called the second wheel of accomplishment for the Great Anointed King;
neighboring enemies cannot inflict harm upon him, and he shall protect his own life, attaining longevity, peace, and happiness.
Thus it is, good son!

When the Tathāgata first attained the Way of the Buddha and realized unsurpassed wisdom, his Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena of the past, future, and present was also like the Dharma-eye attained by all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

Therefore, one practices the True Dharma in order to observe the various characteristics of all karmic retributions; possessing the profound eye of Dharma, one discerns the causes of karma, enabling all roots of goodness to blaze forth and remain secure throughout the long night;
causing all sentient beings to achieve various kinds of immeasurable happiness;
and enabling all externalists and adversaries to submit spontaneously.
"What are the three types of activity? They are:
sitting in meditation, reciting the scriptures, and attending to the affairs of the Sangha.
What is meant by meditation?"
There are ten kinds of dhyāna. What are the ten?
The first is the knowledge of the body;
Knowing the six sense bases of the body;
knowing "self" and "what belongs to self";
and knowing that one undergoes birth through the power of karma as its cause.
One knows the various kinds of craving and the darkness of ignorance;

one knows that what is cherished has no reality, being subject to manifold causes and conditions, and that the stream of suffering flows on without interruption. To extinguish these, one brings them all to total cessation.
"What is the flow of karma? To observe all three types of karmic actions is called the flow of karma.
That which has birth and death as its limit, with craving as the causal condition for existence, is called the flow of afflictions."
Due to the causal conditions of the afflictions, the conjunction with ignorance gives rise to name-and-form;
due to the causal conditions of the conjunction with name-and-form, the six sense bases arise;
and due to the causal conditions of the six sense bases, contact arises.
With contact as condition, feeling arises;
with feeling as condition, renewed existence arises;
with renewed existence as condition, birth arises.
Because of the causal conditions of birth, one is able to give rise to old age, sickness, death, and suffering;
this is called the flow of suffering.
Thus, these three flows all arise from craving.

Why is this? Because ignorance acts as the karma and craving serves as the moisture for these three streams, one contemplates impermanence in order to dry them up; this is called the patience of impermanence.
They are able to contemplate impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self; they believe that all phenomena are ignorant and devoid of wisdom;
like illusions, like mirages, like the moon reflected in water, and like dreams; empty, signless, and wishless;
quiescent, unarisen, and void of all marks.
Constantly contemplate the five aggregates as empty, signless, and wishless;
in accordance with the patience of compliance, joyfully observe the exhalation and inhalation, binding the mindfulness to the breath through increasing and decreasing the count;
observe the abiding, observe the cessation, and observe both the abiding and the cessation.
Furthermore, there are two kinds of counting:
first, when both mind and applied and sustained thought (vitarka-vicāra) have ceased;
second, when one perceives the characteristics of the out-breath and in-breath within applied and sustained thought.
There are two ways of reducing the count:
relying on the emergence [of breath] that can eliminate vitarka and vicāra, one takes up the characteristics of the exhalation and inhalation.
There are two kinds of observing the abiding:
Contemplating the inhalation and exhalation, one perceives the cessation of conceptualization and the mind can abide in meditative concentration.
There are two kinds of cessation:

first, the complete eradication of all fetters and the profound purification of views; second, cultivating the contemplation of the five aggregates through the observation of inhalation and exhalation.
Why is this? These inhalations and exhalations are called the aggregate of the proliferation of form (rūpa-saṃskāra-skandha);
they are also called the aggregates of the proliferation of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness (vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskāra, and vijñāna).
This is called the characteristic of the various non-correspondences of the five aggregates of clinging (*pañca-upādāna-skandha*).
Furthermore, there are five kinds:
not new, not old, not existent, not an accumulation, and not expressible—these are the five kinds.
By means of these five aggregates, one contemplates the three kinds of karma; by means of these three kinds of karma, one contemplates their ultimate exhaustion.
Furthermore, one contemplates the six sense bases: there is "I" and "mine," there is karma, with ignorance as the field and craving as the moisture, until they are ultimately extinguished.

By observing in this way, one fully possesses the four foundations of mindfulness and cultivates them to fulfillment; through the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path, one is able to fulfill even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, attain the patience of non-arising and all-knowledge, and become fully endowed with the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
By practicing the *ānāpāna-smṛti* samādhi of the inhalation and exhalation of breath, one fulfills the dwelling place of all true dharmas (*saddharma*).

If one can thus cultivate these various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna-samādhi*), this constitutes making offerings to all Buddhas of the past and future; such a person is called a son of the Buddha, born from the mouth of the Buddha and born from the true dharma.
Those who are able to cultivate dhyāna well in this manner are either great beings such as the various bodhisattvas,
or those who have exhausted their outflows, such as pratyekabuddhas and arhats, according to what they have cultivated and accumulated;
these are called bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who are then able to fulfill the eighteen unique qualities and possess all-knowledge.
“Good son! This person shall before long attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; they are also the profound Dharma-eye of the Tathāgatas, the World-Honored Ones, of the three periods of time.”
Fulfilling karmic actions and observing their retributions, they establish sentient beings in ten kinds of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
In this way, noble son, one is able to turn the wheel of dharma of meditative concentration turned by the Tathāgata.
"Good son, how does one cultivate the recitation and study of the Tathāgata?
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, good son!"

There are those with slight faith and meager roots of goodness whose roots have not yet matured within the context of conventional truth; for the sake of such sentient beings, one should practice recitation and cultivate meditative concentration at the beginning, middle, and end of the night, seeking supreme wisdom with joyful diligence.

At that time, I established others in the Mahāyāna, practicing meditative concentration, reciting, receiving, and upholding the teachings, and making various offerings; I recited them myself and taught others to recite, spoke them myself and taught others to speak, made offerings myself and taught others to make offerings, and established myself in the Mahāyāna while also teaching others to abide in the Mahāyāna, mutually instructing and transforming one another to extinguish all afflictions.

All this was for the sake of attaining the benefit of the unsurpassed path, desiring to extinguish the immeasurable sufferings of all sentient beings, and to attain entry into the city of nirvāṇa, the realm of fearlessness.
If there are sentient beings who delight in seeking the state of a pratyekabuddha, he preaches for them the Dharma of the twelve links of dependent origination.

To those who delight in seeking the state of a śrāvaka, he preaches the hundreds of thousands of teachings of the four Āgamas, as well as the immeasurable Abhidharma and other doctrines, causing them to recite, study, and practice according to what has been taught.
"Good son! This is called the Tathāgata’s wheel of cultivation, recitation, and practice. Good son!"

If there are sentient beings of dull faculties who, for the sake of giving rise to the causes and conditions for roots of goodness, are indolent, possess little wisdom, and have lost right mindfulness; who are greedily attached to their dwellings, robes, food, drink, and the four types of material offerings, and remain far removed from all spiritual friends—such beings, O son of good family!
should be taught and exhorted to manage the affairs of the Saṃgha and the Buddha-dharma for the sake of their preceptors and ācāryas.
This constitutes the meritorious ground of establishing the Tathāgata, exhorting others, and performing supportive services.
In this way, son of good family, one truly knows the dharma of practicing cultivation.
Son of good family!

This is called the second Buddha-wheel: the wheel of maturing sentient beings through the perfection of the three karmas. It reaches the state of peace and fearlessness, enabling the lion’s roar and the turning of the Brahma-wheel of Dharma, whereby all external adversaries are completely subdued, and one is able to know the causes and conditions of sentient beings as they truly are.
“Good son! It is like a consecrated Kṣatriya king who carefully observes among śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, and śūdras who possesses courage and skill, who is learned and observant of the precepts;

who knows well how to distinguish those with merit, who possesses skillful means and wisdom, who is able to exert diligent effort with firm resolve without retreating, and who adorns himself with various kinds of merit.”

Thereupon, among the assembly, he was consecrated as a Kṣatriya king; in accordance with his status, gold, silver, precious jewels, granaries, treasuries, fine silks, as well as all fields, houses, slaves, and servants, were all bestowed upon him as the property of this kingdom.
If there are those among sentient beings who are able to maintain the precepts, such beings are also provided for when they are in need or lacking.

If there are sentient beings who do not maintain the precepts—those with little diligence, who are indolent, lazy, and forgetful of right mindfulness; who lack a heart of compassion and gratitude; and who, fearing nothing of future lives, remain mired in the mud of desire—[the Bodhisattva likewise provides for them].

In this way, the consecrated Kṣatriya great king, according to the specific circumstances of each case, inflicts punishment or offers consolation; he may punish by means of commands, or punish by means of imprisonment, or punish by means of fines; furthermore, there may be the confiscation of various properties, or the infliction of flogging, or the amputation of limbs, or the decapitation of the head—there are such immeasurable methods of instruction as these.
This is called the third wheel of the consecrated Kṣatriya great king.
"It can cause one's own realm to flourish, subdue all evil external enemies, and protect one's life-force so that one attains longevity. 'So it is, so it is!'"

"Good son! If my śrāvaka disciples lack wisdom, skillful means, merit, and the various methods of discipline; if they forget right mindfulness, have distracted minds, and are negligent, yet take refuge in me—I know their fundamental nature and discipline them according to their characteristics."

If there are those who are arrogant and difficult to subdue, whose minds lack reverence and who do not steadfastly uphold the precepts, one shall subdue them for the sake of the long-term endurance of the Dharma.

If they give rise to such thoughts, one should instruct them to repent; furthermore, if it is necessary to reprimand them with words, one should drive them to humble their pride and never speak with them again.
